newsitem.title: CANADA: Falconbridge CEO dies during Chile visit.
newsitem.headline: Falconbridge CEO dies during Chile visit.

text.p: Canadian miner Falconbridge Ltd. said on Wednesday that President and Chief Executive Officer Frank Pickard died of natural causes in Chile.
Pickard, 63, died during a visit to the Falconbridge's joint-venture Collahuasi copper site in northern Chile, the Toronto-based company said in a statement.
A company spokeswoman said the board of directors would meet soon to discuss Pickard's replacement.
Earlier this year, Pickard led a C$4.1 billion ($3 billion) takeover bid for junior miner Diamond Fields Resources Inc. and its prized Voisey's Bay nickel deposit in Labrador in northeastern Canada.
But Falconbridge was defeated by a richer C$4.3 billion offer ($3.2 billion) from rival mining giant Inco Ltd.
Pickard is the second Canadian mining chief executive to die in recent months.
Lawrie Reinertson, former president and chief executive officer of Rio Algom Ltd., died of a heart attack in July.
Falconbridge is the western world's third-largest nickel producer and is owned 43.6 percent by Toronto-based Noranda Inc.
